conviction_note: Scale: 11.5 (the event-implied move is 11.3 and the name's last 8 prints have a median of 7.2, one of them -24.8). The lean is slightly positive: the company beat its own EPS guide by a wide margin in Q1 and Q2, the stock fell 12.9% in 5 sessions with no company news, the skew bids calls, and peers and mall traffic look firm. Against that, the Q4 holiday guide is the line this stock trades on and consensus already sits at the top of the Q3 guide and in the upper half of the FY guide. Net p_up 54, so (2*0.54-1)*11.5 = +0.92. impact_sum +1.2 is close to this and both are small against an 11% implied move.
bar: Company Q3 2026 guide (8-K ex.99.1, 2026-08-26, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000701985/000070198526000025/ex991bbwi-20262qearningsre.htm): net sales -5% to -2.5% vs $1,594M (about $1,514-1,554M), adjusted EPS $0.07-0.12, GAAP EPS $0.05-0.10, including a ~$0.03 loss on debt repurchased on 2026-08-19, no buybacks assumed. FY2026 adjusted EPS $2.60-2.80, net sales -4% to -2.5%, FCF ~$650M. Street: Q3 adjusted EPS $0.11 (Earnings Whispers via search, https://www.earningswhispers.com/stocks/bbwi; the sweep row says $0.12), so consensus sits at the top of the guide. Revenue consensus -2.7% y/y, about $1,551M (StockStory, 2026-11-18, https://stockstory.org/us/stocks/nyse/bbwi/news/earnings/bath-and-body-works-q3-earnings-report-preview-what-to-look-for), also at the top of the guide. FY adjusted EPS consensus $2.74 (MarketBeat, 2026-11-13, https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/analyst-bath-body-works-nyse-bbwi-price-target-raised-to-2200-2026-11-13/). Derived: implied Q4 consensus is about $1.69 (2.74 - 0.32 Q1 - 0.62 Q2 - 0.11 Q3) against a Q4 2025 adjusted figure of about $2.00 (FY25 adjusted 3.21 less 0.49 + 0.37 + 0.35). The guide makes the bar sourced; the exact EPS consensus has one or two sources ($0.11 / $0.12).
positioning_check: Short interest: about 7.8% of float (Benzinga sentiment page, undated, https://www.benzinga.com/quote/BBWI/sentiment). Days to cover 2.44 at the 2026-05-15 settlement, 2.25 at 2026-06-30 (curvedtrading, https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/bbwi/), 3.3 per equibles (undated). Borrow fee 0.4%. No November 2026 settlement found. Not a crowded short. Options (sealed baseline): 25d skew -4.91 vol points, so calls are bid ('upside paid'); put/call OI 0.41; event-implied move 11.3%, straddle 11.89%, ATM IV 164%. Tape: -12.87% over 5 days and -7.32% over 20 days, -9.91% on 2026-11-16 with no company news while the S&P fell 1.92% (https://cappnotes.substack.com/p/closing-look-monday-november-16-2026), $21.43 on 11-13 against $18.93 spot. Institutions own 95%. Sell side: 15 Hold, 4 Buy, 1 Sell. Recent targets: UBS raised to $22 from $17 (11-13), Wells Fargo $25 Overweight (10-29).

findings.finding: The stock went into the print down 12.9% in 5 sessions ($21.43 on 2026-11-13 to $18.93 on 11-18), including -9.9% on 2026-11-16, the worst name in the S&P 500 that day, with no company news. It now trades below its 200-day average. That resets the bar the market holds below the sell-side numbers, which have not moved (UBS raised its target to $22 on 11-13).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last three prints (2026-03, 05, 08) went +2.6, +9.7 and +7.5 on beats of a low guide. The 2025-11 print, which carried a holiday-guide cut, went -24.8. The baseline records no pre-print drawdown of this size.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced by construction, because the drop is the price. What the market may not have reflected is that a holder de-risking into the print leaves a lower whisper than the $0.11-0.12 and -2.7% consensus. Had the sell side moved down with it, we would see estimate cuts and target cuts this week; instead the only action was UBS raising to $22.
findings.independence: The tape is in the sealed baseline (run_up_5d -12.87%). The cause cannot be explained: https://cappnotes.substack.com/p/closing-look-monday-november-16-2026 lists BBWI -9.91% with no reason given. The calls-bid skew in the baseline is consistent with it. An unexplained drawdown is a weak signal.

findings.finding: Under the current team BBWI has guided low and then beaten its own EPS range by a wide margin: Q2 2026 adjusted EPS was $0.31 excluding refunds (and $0.62 reported) against a $0.20-0.25 guide, and Q1 2026 was $0.32 against roughly $0.29 consensus. Q2 sales of $1,514M also beat the roughly $1,500M expected. The Q3 guide is $0.07-0.12, with consensus at the top ($0.11-0.12), so only a beat above the range is new.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 beat of guide: +7.51. Q1 2026 beat: +9.70. Q4 2025 beat: +2.59 (another source says shares fell 8% intraday on 2026-03-05 on the guide).
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus at the top of the guide already prices a beat to the upper end. What is not priced is a repeat of the Q2-size beat of about $0.06 ex-refund over the guide top. If that were priced, consensus would sit above $0.12, and it does not.
findings.independence: The Q1 numbers come from a different document (https://investors.bbwinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/bath-body-works-reports-first-quarter-results-exceeding-guidance, 2026-05-27). Same management team, so these are one pattern, not two facts.

findings.finding: Mall traffic was firm through BBWI's Q3 (Aug-Oct). Placer.ai's October 2026 Mall Index shows indoor malls +4.1% y/y (open-air +5.8%, outlets +3.6%), with September also up across all formats and August 'indoor malls' best YoY growth of 2026'. This is set against a Q3 guide of sales -2.5% to -5%. About 40% of BBWI's fleet is in malls.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Transmission is weak: in Q2 2026 BBWI's own Placer visits were -0.2% y/y while US/Canada store sales fell 5.4%, and mall traffic was positive then too.
findings.why_not_priced: Mall indices are public, but nobody aggregates them into BBWI's numbers. Placer says October had an extra Saturday, a calendar help. If the market priced firm traffic as a sales beat, revenue consensus would sit above the guide top; at -2.7% it sits at it.
findings.independence: Proxy. BBWI-specific Placer data through July 2026 shows visits flat (https://www.placer.ai/anchor/articles/beauty-traffic-defies-a-tough-consumer-environment, 2026-08-26). The NRF/CNBC Retail Monitor had October retail sales +3.57% y/y (search snippet, homepagenews/NRF 2026-11-11).

findings.finding: Peers that reported after BBWI last spoke were mixed to firm. TJX's Q3 FY27 (quarter to 2026-10-31) comps were +4% against a +2-3% guide, and its EPS included a $0.05 tariff-refund benefit. Sally Beauty revenue was flat and in line, stock -1.4%. Warby Parker revenue was in line, stock +19.7%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No measured read-through history. In 2025-11 BBWI fell 24.8% the day before TJX/TGT beats, which suggests its own guide dominates peer reads.
findings.why_not_priced: TJX printed hours before this seal, and an off-price consumer read has not reached BBWI estimates. If it had, the Q3 consensus would have moved this week, and no revision is visible.
findings.independence: Sally and Warby reactions: StockStory preview (https://stockstory.org/us/stocks/nyse/bbwi/news/earnings/bath-and-body-works-q3-earnings-report-preview-what-to-look-for, 2026-11-18). Different businesses; proxy only.

findings.finding: Further IEEPA tariff refunds may have landed in BBWI's Q3. Q2 adjusted EPS included about $80M of refunds 'received in the quarter', and the Q3/FY outlook text is silent on further refunds. Counterparties show refunds were still flowing in Aug-Oct 2026: TJX's Q3 EPS includes a $0.05 refund benefit. BBWI has put refunds inside adjusted EPS, so any residual would show in the headline against a $0.07-0.12 bar ($10M is about $0.04/share after tax).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (the refund quarter) went +7.51, but the release paired the refund with a raised FY guide. Peers' refund-padded beats were discounted (Ford fell on a refund-driven beat, per Supply Chain Dive coverage).
findings.why_not_priced: No source quantifies a remaining BBWI refund, and consensus at $0.11-0.12 sits inside the guide, consistent with no refund being modelled. If one were modelled, consensus would sit above the guide top. Either way it is a one-off with no path to the Q4 guide.
findings.independence: TJX refund benefit in Q3: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000109198/000010919826000058/tjxq3fy27earningspressrele.htm. CBP says refunds take 60-90 days after a declaration is accepted (https://www.supplychaindive.com/news/what-off-price-retailers-are-saying-about-tariff-refunds/829450/).

findings.finding: The holiday Q4 guide is the risk line. FY adjusted guide $2.60-2.80 less Q1 $0.32, Q2 $0.62 and Q3 $0.07-0.12 implies Q4 of about $1.54-1.79. Street FY $2.74 implies about $1.69, upper half, against about $2.00 in Q4 2025. Excluding the ~$0.30 Q2 refund, the raised FY guide is about $2.30-2.50, at or below the bottom of the original $2.40-2.65. So the underlying business was guided down, and Q3 carries about 70% of a ~$35M incremental marketing spend ahead of the holiday.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2025-11-20: Q4 guide cut and transformation plan, -24.81. 2026-03 FY guide: +2.59 close-to-close but -8% intraday on the guide. 2026-08: FY raised (on the refund), +7.51.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus at $2.74 sits in the upper half of a range that is itself refund-padded. A holiday guide that holds the FY range but narrows it to the midpoint ($2.70) is a cut to the Street. If that were priced, FY consensus would sit at or below $2.70. The 5-day drawdown may be part of this pricing, so the size is kept small.
findings.independence: Q1 actuals: https://investors.bbwinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/bath-body-works-reports-first-quarter-results-exceeding-guidance. Marketing-investment timing: Kalkine search snippet (https://kalkine.ca/news/retail/why-does-bath-body-works-nysebbwi-expect-only-usd-007-through-usd-012-per-share-this-quarter). FY consensus: MarketBeat 2026-11-13. Q4'25 is derived arithmetic.

findings.finding: Capital return is unused optionality. Cash was $794M at end Q2 (vs $364M a year earlier), there have been no buybacks YTD (vs $254M in H1 2025), the outlook 'assumes no share repurchases', FY FCF is ~$650M, and the stock trades at ~5.6x P/E (MarketBeat). The company chose to repurchase debt on 2026-08-19. A buyback restart announced with the print would be new.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No recent buyback announcement at a print to compare against.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus excludes buybacks per the guide. If the market expected a restart, Street FY EPS would sit above the guide range. At $2.74 it does not. The probability is unknown, since the company has been prioritising debt reduction.
findings.independence: Balance-sheet table: https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/BBWI/8-k-bath-body-works-inc-reports-material-event-33bc6d64576c.html. Same 8-K, so not independent.

findings.finding: The finance seat is still interim and the CEO's pay now rides on the share price. A Form 4 dated 2026-11-10 grants interim CFO Tom Javitch a one-time RSU (11,547 shares, vesting 40/60 over two years), so no permanent CFO has been named. An 8-K of 2026-09-23 granted CEO Heaf a $10M target PSU (591,366 shares, implying about $16.91 a share) earned only at 60-day average prices of $40/$60/$80/$100.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The CFO exit was disclosed with Q1 on 2026-05-27, and the stock rose 9.7 that day.
findings.why_not_priced: Interim status is known (it is in the wire). A permanent CFO named with the print would be new; none is signalled. The PSU hurdles say little about one quarter.
findings.independence: CEO PSU 8-K: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/701985/000119312526399454/d130416d8k.htm (2026-09-23). A director's fractional sale on 2026-10-16 (doc4.xml in 0001225208-26-008479) is noise.

baseline_tension: Mild agreement with the skew (calls bid, -4.9) and against the 5-day run-up (-12.9%): the small positive lean says the drawdown reset the bar while consensus did not. The guidance risk keeps it near a coin flip.
lessons_applied: Lesson 5 (an unexplained drawdown is not a cause): the positioning finding on the -12.9% 5-day fall cut from +1.0 to +0.3, still filed; p_up 55 -> 54.
Lesson 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction): the beat-of-guide pattern cut from +1.0 to +0.8, because consensus already sits at the guide top and only a beat above it is new.
Lesson 2 (one-offs as one-offs): the residual tariff refund cut from +0.3 to +0.2, since it has no path to the Q4 guide.

Lessons 6 and 7 left the guidance finding (-1.0) and the mall/peer proxies (+0.3 each) unchanged: the bar is sourced to the company guide, short interest is not crowded and the negative does not oppose the skew much.
